# Windows and WSL: reference

Inspect and repair WSL, and read the Windows host from inside it. The guide is [README.md](README.md); this page lists every function, alias and command, as their own help prints it (`gash_help NAME`, `gash COMMAND --help`).

## Functions

| Function | Alias | Description |
|---|---|---|
| [`wsl_compact`](#wsl_compact) | `wslc` | Fix Windows interop on a WSL2 VM with fragmented memory |
| [`wsl_explorer`](#wsl_explorer) | `wex` | Open Windows Explorer from WSL |
| [`wsl_restart`](#wsl_restart) | `wr` | Restart WSL (saves history, runs wsl --shutdown) |
| [`wsl_shutdown`](#wsl_shutdown) | `wsd` | Shutdown WSL (saves history, runs wsl --shutdown) |
| [`wsl_taskmanager`](#wsl_taskmanager) | `wtm` | Open Windows Task Manager from WSL |

### wsl_compact

Fix Windows interop on a WSL2 VM with fragmented memory.

Alias: `wslc`

#### Usage

```text
wsl_compact [--status] [-y]
```

#### Examples

```bash
# code . or explorer.exe fail with "UtilAcceptVsock ... accept4 failed 110"
wslc

# Only show the failures and the free large blocks, change nothing
wslc --status
```

#### Notes

```text
Every Windows program started from WSL needs a contiguous 512 KiB block
of guest memory for its hv_sock channel. When memory is fragmented the
allocation fails (dmesg: "page allocation failure: order:7") and the
launch times out. wsl_compact drops the page cache and slab, compacts
memory (sudo), prints the free blocks before and after, and checks that
cmd.exe starts. If it still fails, run `wsl --shutdown` from Windows.
On a terminal it runs without asking; headless it needs -y (--yes).
Unattended, sudo must not need a password (sudo -n is checked first).
When dmesg is not readable the failure count is "unknown".
```

See also: [`wsl_restart`](../windows/reference.md#wsl_restart), [`wsl_shutdown`](../windows/reference.md#wsl_shutdown)

### wsl_explorer

Open Windows Explorer from WSL.

Alias: `wex`

#### Usage

```text
wsl_explorer [PATH]
```

#### Examples

```bash
# Open Explorer in current directory
wex

# Open Explorer in a specific path
wex /home/user/projects

# Open Explorer in Windows user folder
wex /mnt/c/Users
```

#### Notes

```text
Defaults to current directory if no path specified.
Only works inside WSL (Windows Subsystem for Linux).
```

See also: [`wsl_taskmanager`](../windows/reference.md#wsl_taskmanager)

### wsl_restart

Restart WSL (saves history, runs wsl --shutdown).

Alias: `wr`

#### Usage

```text
wsl_restart [-y]
```

#### Examples

```bash
# Restart WSL (asks, saves bash history first)
wr

# Without the question
wr -y
```

#### Notes

```text
Runs `wsl --shutdown`: every distro stops, Docker Desktop's included,
with the servers running in them. WSL starts again with the next
terminal. Asks first; -y skips the question. Same as wsl_shutdown.
```

See also: [`wsl_shutdown`](../windows/reference.md#wsl_shutdown)

### wsl_shutdown

Shutdown WSL (saves history, runs wsl --shutdown).

Alias: `wsd`

#### Usage

```text
wsl_shutdown [-y]
```

#### Examples

```bash
# Shut down WSL (asks, saves bash history first)
wsd
```

#### Notes

```text
Runs `wsl --shutdown`: every distro stops, Docker Desktop's included.
Asks first; -y skips the question.
```

See also: [`wsl_restart`](../windows/reference.md#wsl_restart)

### wsl_taskmanager

Open Windows Task Manager from WSL.

Alias: `wtm`

#### Usage

```text
wsl_taskmanager
```

#### Examples

```bash
# Open Windows Task Manager
wtm
```

#### Notes

```text
Launches Task Manager in the background.
Does not change your current working directory.
Only works inside WSL (Windows Subsystem for Linux).
```

See also: [`wsl_explorer`](../windows/reference.md#wsl_explorer), [`process_find`](../system/reference.md#process_find)

## Commands

### gash wsl

```text
Inspect and repair the WSL distribution and convert paths

Usage:
  gash wsl [flags]
  gash wsl [command]

Available Commands:
  config      Show the effective wsl.conf and .wslconfig settings
  doctor      Check WSL, interop, drives, networking and configuration
  info        A quick summary of the WSL environment
  interop     Report the Windows interop of this shell
  path        Convert a path between its Linux and Windows forms

Flags:
  -h, --help   help for wsl

Use "gash wsl [command] --help" for more information about a command.
```

### gash wsl config

```text
Show the effective wsl.conf and .wslconfig settings

Usage:
  gash wsl config [FILE] [flags]

Flags:
  -h, --help   help for config
      --json   one JSON object on stdout
```

### gash wsl doctor

```text
Check WSL, interop, drives, networking and configuration

Usage:
  gash wsl doctor [flags]

Flags:
  -h, --help   help for doctor
      --json   one JSON object on stdout
```

### gash wsl interop

```text
Report the Windows interop of this shell

Usage:
  gash wsl interop [flags]

Flags:
      --export export WSL_INTEROP=…   print only export WSL_INTEROP=… for eval
  -h, --help                            help for interop
      --json                            one JSON object on stdout
```

### gash wsl path

```text
Convert a path between its Linux and Windows forms

Usage:
  gash wsl path PATH [flags]

Flags:
  -h, --help      help for path
      --json      one JSON object on stdout
      --linux     force the Linux form (/mnt/c/Users/me)
      --mixed     force the Windows form with forward slashes (C:/Users/me)
      --windows   force the Windows form (C:\Users\me)
```

### gash win

```text
Inspect the Windows host from WSL (read-only)

Usage:
  gash win [flags]
  gash win [command]

Available Commands:
  apps        Installed programs (optionally filtered)
  defender    Microsoft Defender status
  disk        Fixed drives with size and free space
  doctor      A composed health check of the Windows host
  events      Windows event log entries
  file        A file's metadata, owner, ACL and signature
  fix         Apply an elevated Windows correction (human-only, asks for UAC)
  hosts       The Windows hosts file
  info        Windows build, edition, host, user and elevation
  net         Network adapters, DNS and proxy
  policy      Where policy is set (registry roots) and the device join
  ports       Listening and established TCP ports with the owning process
  procs       Top processes by memory (optionally filtered)
  reg         Query a registry key (HKLM\…, HKCU\…)
  services    Windows services (optionally filtered by name)
  updates     Installed hotfixes and pending reboot

Flags:
  -h, --help   help for win

Use "gash win [command] --help" for more information about a command.
```

### gash win fix

```text
Apply an elevated Windows correction (human-only, asks for UAC)

Usage:
  gash win fix [ACTION] [ARGS...] [flags]

Flags:
      --dry-run   print the exact elevated command without running it
  -h, --help      help for fix
      --json      with --dry-run, emit the command as JSON
      --yes       skip the in-shell question (Windows still asks for UAC)
```
